sources.locator: DESCRIPTION: a caller that is not a process-group leader can create a new session and process group and becomes their sole initial member. NOTES: forked children inherit the session ID. Direct open was attempted but timed out; the search result exposed these sections.
observed_operation: web.open (timed out; no page body returned)
sources.observed_behavior: setsid() succeeds for a caller that is not already a process-group leader, creating a new session and process group; the caller is initially the only member. A child normally inherits its parent's session ID, but a non-group-leader child can create a separate session/group. Thus signalling only the worker's original process group does not prove all descendants were terminated.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: setsid() fails when the caller is already a process-group leader. A forked child whose PID differs from the inherited process-group ID can meet the non-leader condition. This describes Linux/POSIX process/session semantics; cgroup membership and Windows Job Object behavior are separate mechanisms.
sources.applicability: Directly qualifies the proposal to treat process-group termination as sufficient teardown for an untrusted converter. Use cgroup/job membership or another verified per-platform mechanism for a whole-job guarantee; do not generalize this Linux finding to other platforms.
